questions.q: What does a negative FVA for a step mean?
options: The step made the forecast better
The step made the forecast worse than the previous step

questions.q: WAPE after the statistical step is 0.18 and after the ML step 0.15. What is the FVA of the ML step (in WAPE points, decimal)?
Net savings are 50k per month and the project costs 300k. What is the payback in months?
Scenario: planners override 30% of forecasts and the overrides have negative FVA on average, but positive FVA for new store openings. What do you do?
options: Keep overrides for events the model cannot know and reduce the rest, with feedback to planners
why: Correct: use FVA by type of override.

questions.q: Which assumption usually moves ROI the most?
options: The cost per unit of error and the adoption rate

questions.q: Why compare to a baseline in an ROI case?
options: Savings are the difference to what would happen without the project

questions.q: Scenario: a finance partner asks 'why should I believe 3 points of WAPE are worth 1M?' Best answer:
options: Show the cost factor, its source (a pilot or history of waste and stock-outs), a cautious range and the plan to measure it
